title.value: Coordination Among Neural Modules Through A Shared Global Workspace
title.justification: The title is directly mentioned in the beginning of the paper and reflects the main focus of the research work.
title.quote:
Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2022.

C OORDINATION A MONG N EURAL M ODULES T HROUGH A S HARED G LOBAL W ORKSPACE

analysis.description: The paper explores a method for coordinating interactions among neural modules in deep learning models by using a shared global workspace. This approach is inspired by the Global Workspace Theory from cognitive neuroscience, and aims to improve the coherence and synchronization of specialist modules. By allowing these modules to communicate via a shared workspace with limited bandwidth, the paper demonstrates improved specialization, compositionality, and synchronization, enhancing performance in complex tasks.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments and performance comparisons across various tasks, demonstrating the practical utility of the proposed method, which characterizes empirical research.
type.quote: The experiments have the following goals: (a) Demonstrate that the use of the shared workspace can improve results on a wide array of challenging benchmark tasks, with the goal of demonstrating the practical utility and breadth of the technique.

name.justification: The research is focused on the coordination of neural modules within architectures like Transformers using a shared workspace, which aligns with the field of Neural Architecture.
name.quote: We explore the use of such a communication channel in the context of deep learning for modeling the structure of complex environments.

name.justification: The paper extends the Transformer model by adding a shared workspace to improve coherence and synchronization.
name.quote: We extend the Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017), attention and slot-based modular architectures by adding a shared workspace and allowing modules (each representing an entity) to compete for write access in each computational stage.

name.justification: The usage of attention mechanisms is central to enabling module interactions within the shared workspace framework.
name.quote: Both Transformers and RIMs utilize a self-attention mechanism for sharing information between modules, typically implemented in a pairwise manner.

name.justification: These are specific architectures that use the proposed shared workspace for improved task performance.
name.quote: We investigate a neural architecture reminiscent of the GW model, where a number of sparsely communicating specialist modules interact via a shared working memory.
